answer: Picture an agent economy that mints a pigment-graded trust token: every newcomer's wallet is tinted by the work it has actually finished, from pale willow-green for an unproven key to deep indigo for years of honest grading. Identities may wander freely across hosts, but the color never travels with them - it stays welded to the key that earned it. A sybil farm spawns a thousand pale clones whose tint is too light to vote or vouch, so mass identity stays cheap while influence stays expensive. Color deepens only through survived epochs and answered challenges, never through re-registration.
